title: Engineering Adherent Bacteria by Creating a Single Synthetic Curli Operon
protocol: Determine the genetic organization and localize the endogenous transcriptional and translational signals of the curli genes.
Gather information from specialized databases such as RegulonDB or EcoGene.
Complete data with a careful reading of pertinent publications.
Perform data management and in silico preanalysis using Clone Manager software.
Select the coding sequences for five required genes: csgB, csgA, csgE, csgF, and csgG.
Extract chosen sequences from the database in FASTA format.
Convert the antisense csgGFE cluster into its reverse complement counterpart using Clone Manager tools.
Ligate the csgEFG sequence behind the csgBA sequence.
Add the promoter Prcn in front of the csgBAEFG chimerical sequence.
Optimize transcriptional signals by adding a perfect ribosome binding site (AAGGAGGTATATA) before the first ATG of the csgBA DNA sequence.
Add another perfect ribosome binding site before the csgEFG sequence.
Maintain endogenous RBS for csgB, csgF, and csgG genes.
Flank the device with a standard BioBrick prefix containing EcoRI and PstI restriction sites.
Flank the device with a standard BioBrick suffix containing SpeI and XbaI restriction sites.
Eliminate EcoRI, PstI, SpeI, and XbaI recognition sites in the device.
Modify a PstI site in the csgA sequence located at position 80 to CGTCTG.
Modify another PstI site in the rcnR sequence located at position 1340 to CAGCAG.
Modify an EcoRI site in the csgE gene located at position 1830 to GAATT.
Run translation simulation using Clone Manager software.
Verify perfect homology between wild type curli protein and proteins encoded by the synthetic operon using BLAST.
Order the synthetic operon from a commercial gene synthesis service provider such as Genecust.
Insert 4 μg of the artificial operon (3165 bp) into pUC57 to create pIG2.
Fill each well of a 24-well polystyrene plate with 2 ml of M63 minimal medium (glucose 0.2%).
Inoculate each well with 10^6 cells of an overnight culture.
Grow bacteria at 30 °C for 18 to 48 hours without shaking.
Add the proper amount of cobalt (25 to 100 mM) and antibiotic (ampicillin 100 μg/L) when needed.
Recover the supernatant containing the planktonic cells from each well.
Rinse each well with 1 ml of M63 and pool the rinse with the initial supernatant obtained.
Scrape and pipette up and down to recover the biofilm in 1 ml of M63.
Vortex the mixture for 15 seconds.
Estimate the number of surface-attached and swimming bacteria from the optical density at 600 nm (OD600).
Calculate the adherence percentage using the formula: Bx100/(3xS+B).
Discard planktonic cells in the last row of the 24-well plate.
Rinse with 1 ml of M63 the biofilm which had developed on the bottom of the plate in the last row.
Dry the open plate for 1 hour at 80 °C.
Add 100 μl of 20% crystal violet for 2 min in each well followed by extensive washes with water.
Introduce 3 rectangular glass coverslip in each Petri dish.
Incubate overnight at 30 °C without shaking.
Remove the coverslip from the Petri dish.
Drain the coverslip carefully.
Clean the lower face of the coverslip with a small cotton swab impregnated with 70% ethanol to remove bacterial residue.
For confocal observation, clean both upper ends of the sample on a few millimeters.
Deposit the cleaned coverslip on a glass slide with the biofilm side facing up.
Cover the biofilm with a larger coverslip fixed to the glass slide with varnish.
Invert the setup so that the biofilm is now on the lower face.
Place the inverted setup under the confocal laser microscope.
Excite GFP at 488 nm for fluorescence excitation.
Collect bacterial fluorescence in the range of 500 to 600 nm.
Use a 40x oil immersion objective for imaging in laser scanning confocal mode.
Scan three-dimensional structures of the biofilms from the solid surface to the interface with the growth medium using a step of 1 μm.
Perform three-dimensional projections with IMARIS software.
Determine biofilm thickness by analyzing the average z value along statistical longitudinal sections.
Quantify biofilm biovolumes from confocal z-stacks as described elsewhere.
